title: Is That 'Windows Tech Support' Call a Scam?
description: Scott Aurnou (http://www.thesecurityadvocate.com/) - Computer Security Tip of the Week: If you receive an unsolicited phone call from someone claiming to be from 'Windows Tech Support' or something like it, you can be sure of one thing: it's a scam.  Learn more about it here.

asr.full_text: Hi there. This is Scott Arnall with this week's security tip . Today, we're going to talk about phone scams. Yes, they still exist generally will start off as an unsolicited phone call from something like window tech support. It might be something similar but that's the general idea they will pretend to be affiliated with a major company and They call may even appear to be local, but it's not. It's coming from somewhere else. Often, it's India There's number of companies that do it out there And that's a process called spoof, where it appears to be something else but it's not. Now what they do is claim that they're alerted to a problem with your PC, generally they try this on Windows based computers and then they'll talk you through the steps, basically making you go do it for them, and you wind up eventually with a screen that looks really scary with all these warnings on it. It's scary, but it's harmless, it's called the Windows Event Manager. It's really nothing. And then they will offer to fix the problem, which of course is a terrible problem, remotely. This is an extremely bad idea. What they'll do is they'll charge you to fix the problem. To fix it, they will either download free software or simply enact stuff on your own computer. And then they'll want to sell you long-term protection. None of this is doing anything to your computer, there is no problem with it at all. If anything they may even try and steal data from you while you're there. Your basic defense is a simple one. Anytime you get an unsolicited call like this, just assume it's a scam, because trust me, they're not really monitoring you like that. None of the companies are. If you assume it's a scam, play it safe. Thanks so much for your time and if you have any questions about this, or other areas of computer security, please feel free to contact us at thesecurityadvocate.com. Thanks so much for your time. Have a great week.
